_comment: C6-8 正文英译 · 1password-mcp（2026-10-31）。八维+mcp 三维+runs/unknowns/related/sources 全键非空。

axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — a local server (stdio, running inside the 1Password desktop app) called by MCP clients.
Its distinctive design is that **the security boundary sits on the server side**: the agent manages Environments
(the secrets-holding containers), but by design the server **never returns secret values to the client** —
the agent only ever sees variable names and environment names.
axes.runtime:
A **local stdio server riding inside the 1Password desktop app** (official docs: it runs locally as part of the 1Password desktop app);
launch command `1password-mcp` (client configuration) or registration via the official plugins
(Claude Code /plugin install, the Cursor plugin marketplace, Codex/Kiro lines of their own).
**The MCP client must support stdio — remote-only clients are not supported** (stated plainly by the official docs).
The companion plugin repos are active (codex-plugin pushed 2026-10-29, claude-plugin pushed 2026-10-29).
axes.local_files:
It can create **locally mounted .env files** — secrets become available to processes on demand without writing them to disk
(official wording); this is its only "local surface", and it is a controlled mount rather than free read/write.
axes.background:
No standalone background process — the server rides the 1Password desktop app and the MCP client session; when 1Password locks,
the authorization window closes (an approval stays valid "until 1Password locks" without re-prompting).
axes.context:
No server-side cross-session memory; state lives in 1Password cloud Environments (cross-device sync is a 1Password account capability,
not MCP-server memory). Approvals are granted per Environment.
axes.permissions:
**The permission model is the core of this dossier**: each sensitive operation triggers a **secure authorization prompt** in the 1Password desktop app
(per-Environment approval); Enterprise admins can toggle the Local MCP server feature wholesale under Policies > Agentic permissions.
Requires a 1Password account + the desktop app + an existing Environment. Beta stage (marked by the official docs).
axes.fit:
Fits: letting coding agents (Claude Code/Codex/Cursor/Kiro) manage the "environment side" of dev secrets — create environments,
add variables, mount .env — while the agent never touches plaintext secrets; governable by enterprises (policy toggle + audit).
Not a fit: agents reading secret values at runtime (impossible by design); remote-only MCP clients (stdio required);
scenarios outside the 1Password ecosystem.

mcp.transport:
**stdio** (command: 1password-mcp; rides the 1Password desktop app); the official plugin lines (Claude Code plugin/MCPB,
Cursor plugin, Kiro Power) register the configuration for you.
Verified: developer.1password.com/docs/environments/mcp-server (200 direct on 2026-10-31, 301 to www.1password.dev, same page).
mcp.auth:
A 1Password account + desktop-app sign-in; sensitive operations pop an authorization window per Environment (an approval lasts until 1Password locks);
Enterprise policy toggle (Policies > Agentic permissions). There is no API-token concept.
mcp.scope:
The Environments management surface (create/list/rename/add variables/mount .env); **no secret-value read surface** (by design);
the local surface is only the controlled .env mount. Among the most conservative permission surfaces of credential-class MCPs.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The beta-to-GA timeline and capability changes (marked beta officially, no public roadmap)
- The capability division between Environments and the 1Password SDK / service accounts / Credential Broker (multiple lines coexist on the developer site; not compared item by item)
- The audit-log export surface of authorization prompts (the enterprise narrative mentions audit; the concrete export format was not verified)
related: The two poles of permission surfaces: Playwright grants the browser full power, 1Password deliberately withholds even secret values — two official answers to "what may an agent touch".
One of the host surfaces of the official plugin line (/plugin install 1password@1password registers the MCP configuration).
